name: Spouse or Child of Japanese National / Permanent Resident visa (日本人の配偶者等 / 永住者の配偶者等)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being the legal spouse of a Japanese national or permanent resident, or their biological/adopted child, in a genuine, ongoing marital relationship.
This requires evidence of a genuine, cohabiting marital relationship — Japanese authorities scrutinise marriages of convenience closely.

evidence_required.document: Marriage certificate, registered in Japan (koseki registration where the Japanese spouse is the sponsor) or apostilled foreign marriage certificate
Evidence of genuine cohabitation and relationship

outcome.duration_length: 6 months, 1 year, 3 years, or 5 years, renewable

sources.title: Immigration Services Agency of Japan — 日本人の配偶者等 (Spouse or Child of Japanese National) visa

notes: Unrestricted work rights — confirmed, no field-of-work limitation the way most sponsored work visas carry, a genuine advantage worth surfacing prominently, similar to the unrestricted-work-rights pattern seen on most other countries' spouse-of-citizen routes in this dataset. No income/sponsorship requirement for the Japanese spouse — unlike UK's Family/Spouse route (£29,000 minimum income) or Spain's family reunification (IPREM-based threshold), Japan imposes no minimum income test on this route at all, a real and confirmed structural simplicity. pr_after_months (36) reflects the commonly-cited accelerated path available to spouses of Japanese nationals (roughly 1-3 years of marriage/residence depending on case specifics) rather than the standard 10-year track — the exact precise cutoff (1 year vs 3 years depending on which factors apply) was not fully disambiguated at tier-1 precision during this research pass, encoded as the more conservative 3-year figure rather than asserting the faster 1-year figure as universally applicable, an honest approximation flagged rather than overclaimed.
